arxiv-1810-11310.title: Periodic paths on the pentagon, double pentagon and golden L
arxiv-1810-11310.creator: Diana Davis, Samuel Lelièvre
arxiv-1810-11310.description: Abstract We give a tree structure on the set of all periodic directions on the golden L, which gives an associated tree structure on the set of periodic directions for the pentagon billiard table and double pentagon surface. We use this to give the periods of periodic directions on the pentagon and double pentagon.

arxiv-2103-06080.title: An exponential integrator/WENO discretization for sonic-boom simulation on modern computer hardware
arxiv-2103-06080.creator: L. Einkemmer, A. Ostermann, M. Residori
arxiv-2103-06080.description: Abstract Recently a splitting approach has been presented for the simulation of sonic-boom propagation. Splitting methods allow one to divide complicated partial differential equations into simpler parts that are solved by specifically tailored numerical schemes. The present work proposes a second order exponential integrator for the numerical solution of sonic-boom propagation modelled through a dispersive equation with Burgers’ nonlinearity.

arxiv-2206-08611.title: Medical Dialogue Response Generation with Pivotal Information Recalling Conference: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 14–18, 2022; Washington, DC, USA Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD
arxiv-2206-08611.creator: Yu Zhao, Yunxin Li, Yuxiang Wu, Baotian Hu, Qingcai Chen, Xiaolong Wang, Yuxin Ding, Min Zhang
arxiv-2206-08611.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yu Zhao, Yunxin Li, Yuxiang Wu, Baotian Hu, Qingcai Chen, Xiaolong Wang, Yuxin Ding, Min Zhang. Medical dialogue generation is an important yet challenging task. Most previous works rely on the attention mechanism and large-scale pretrained language models. However, these methods often fail to acquire pivotal information from the long dialogue history to yield an accurate and informative response, due to the fact that the medical entities usually scatters throughout multiple utterances along with the complex relationships between them.

arxiv-2208-02664.title: Makespan Scheduling of Unit Jobs with Precedence Constraints in O ⁡ ( 1.995 n ) O(1.995^{n}) time
arxiv-2208-02664.creator: Jesper Nederlof, Céline M. F. Swennenhuis, Karol Węgrzycki
arxiv-2208-02664.description: Abstract In a classical scheduling problem, we are given a set of n n jobs of unit length along with precedence constraints and the goal is to find a schedule of these jobs on m m identical machines that minimizes the makespan. This problem is well-known to be NP-hard for an unbounded number of machines.

arxiv-2212-05866.description: Abstract As they play an increasingly important role in determining access to credit, credit scoring models are under growing scrutiny from banking supervisors and internal model validators. arxiv-2309-00745.title: Wall-attached convection under strong inclined magnetic fields
arxiv-2309-00745.creator: Shashwat Bhattacharya 1, Thomas Boeck 1, Dmitry Krasnov 1, Jörg Schumacher 1,2
arxiv-2309-00745.description: Abstract We employ a linear stability analysis and direct numerical simulations to study the characteristics of wall-modes in thermal convection in a rectangular box under strong and inclined magnetic fields. The walls of the convection cell are electrically insulated. The stability analysis assumes periodicity in the spanwise direction perpendicular to the plane of the homogeneous magnetic field.

arxiv-2402-10380.description: Abstract . In the evolving landscape of machine learning, the adaptation of pre-trained models through prompt tuning has become increasingly prominent. This trend is particularly observable in the graph domain, where diverse pre-training strategies present unique challenges in developing effective prompt-based tuning methods for graph neural networks.

arxiv-2405-19375.title: Improving global awareness of linkset predictions using Cross-Attentive Modulation tokens
arxiv-2405-19375.creator: Félix Marcoccia, Cédric Adjih, Paul Mühlethaler
arxiv-2405-19375.description: Abstract This work introduces Cross-Attentive Modulation (CAM) tokens, which are tokens whose initial value is learned, gather information through cross-attention, and modulate the nodes and edges accordingly. These tokens are meant to improve the global awareness of link predictions models which, based on graph neural networks, can struggle to capture graph-level features.

arxiv-2405-20797.title: Ovis: Structural Embedding Alignment for Multimodal Large Language Model
arxiv-2405-20797.creator: Shiyin Lu Yang Li Qing-Guo Chen Zhao Xu, Weihua Luo Kaifu Zhang Han-Jia Ye
arxiv-2405-20797.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shiyin Lu Yang Li Qing-Guo Chen Zhao Xu, Weihua Luo Kaifu Zhang Han-Jia Ye. Current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) typically integrate a pre-trained LLM with another pre-trained vision transformer through a connector, such as an MLP, endowing the LLM with visual capabilities.

arxiv-2407-17542.title: End-to-End simulation framework for astronomical spectrographs: SOXS, CUBES and ANDES
arxiv-2407-17542.creator: A. Scaudo, M. Genoni, G. Li Causi, L. Cabona, M. Landoni, S. Campana, P. Schipani, R. Claudi, M. Aliverti, A. Baruffolo, S. Ben-Ami, F. Biondi, G. Capasso, R. Cosentino, F. D’Alessio, P. D’Avanzo, O. Hershko, H. Kuncarayakti, M. Munari, K. Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, G. Pignata, A. Rubin, S. Scuderi
arxiv-2407-17542.description: Abstract We present our numerical simulation approach for the End-to-End (E2E) model applied to various astronomical spectrographs, such as SOXS (ESO-NTT), CUBES (ESO-VLT), and ANDES (ESO-ELT), covering multiple wavelength regions. The E2E model aim at simulating the expected astronomical observations starting from the radiation of the scientific sources (or calibration sources) up to the raw-frame data produced by the detectors.

arxiv-2408-06903.title: Heterogeneity: An Open Challenge for Federated On-board Machine Learning
arxiv-2408-06903.creator: Maria Hartmann, Grégoire Danoy, Pascal Bouvry
arxiv-2408-06903.description: Abstract The design of satellite missions is currently undergoing a paradigm shift from the historical approach of individualised monolithic satellites towards distributed mission configurations, consisting of multiple small satellites. With a rapidly growing number of such satellites now deployed in orbit, each collecting large amounts of data, interest in on-board orbital edge computing is rising.

pmc-10582751.title: Health perception and restorative experience in the therapeutic landscape of urban wetland parks during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-10582751.creator: Jiang Li, Yating Chang, Xiaoxi Cai, Shaobo Liu, You Peng, Tao Feng, Jialing Qi, Yifeng Ji, Yiting Xia, Wenbo Lai
pmc-10582751.description: IntroductionThe effects of restoration and inspiration in the therapeutic landscape of natural environments on visitors during the COVID-19 pandemic have been well-documented. However, less attention has been paid to the heterogeneity of visitor perceptions of health and the potential impacts of experiences in wetland parks with green and blue spaces on visitors’ overall perceived health.

pmc-11493988.title: Optical moiré bound states in the continuum
pmc-11493988.creator: Haoyu Qin, Shaohu Chen, Weixuan Zhang, Huizhen Zhang, Ruhao Pan, Junjie Li, Lei Shi, Jian Zi, Xiangdong Zhang
pmc-11493988.description: Trapping electromagnetic waves within the radiation continuum holds significant implications in the field of optical science and technology. Photonic bound states in the continuum (BICs) present a distinctive approach for achieving this functionality, offering potential applications in laser systems, sensing technologies, and other domains.

pmc-12482336.title: Investigation of potentially zoonotic Rickettsia species in dogs and their attached ticks in Malawi through the lens of One Health
pmc-12482336.creator: Elisha Chatanga, Henson Kainga, John Kothowa, Michael Luwe, Richard Ssuna, Tinotenda Razemba, Laston Chimaliro, Naoki Hayashi, Yuki Ohsugi, Yongjin Qiu, Kyoko Hayashida, Nariaki Nonaka, Ryo Nakao
pmc-12482336.description: BackgroundThe genus Rickettsia in the order Rickettsiales (Alphaproteobacteria) consists of gram-negative obligate intracellular bacteria that infect a wide range of hosts. Epidemiological studies on the occurrence of Rickettsia spp. and their associated tick vectors are essential to understand their distribution, host range, and transmission mechanisms in nature.

pmc-12567271.title: Is General Anesthesia Safe for a Child with Acute Upper Respiratory Tract Infection? A Narrative Review
pmc-12567271.creator: Jowita Rosada-Kurasińska, Alicja Bartkowska-Śniatkowska, Anna Wiernik, Bartłomiej Kociński, Małgorzata Grześkowiak, Maurizio Aricò
pmc-12567271.description: Anesthesia for children with a current respiratory infection or a history of infection within the last two weeks is always associated with a high risk of respiratory complications. However, this risk decreases significantly when the interval between the last symptoms of the infection and the planned anesthesia and medical procedure is extended to at least 2–4 weeks.

pmc-13322244.title: Hierarchical microtopology and phase-specific delivery functionally restore ultralong nerve continuity across species
pmc-13322244.creator: Shuxin Dai, Feiyi Li, Zheheng Bao, Zhuangzhuang Yang, Jin Wang, Lihua Liu, Mengyao Jia, Shuwei Wang, Zijian Zhang, Xinlong Wang, Yantao Zhao, Adam C. Midgley, Yumin Yang, Meng Fan, Deling Kong, Xianhao Dong
pmc-13322244.description: Repairing ultralong peripheral nerve defects remains a major clinical challenge, primarily due to the requirement for regenerative platforms to be capable of integrating spatial guidance with temporally resolved biochemical cues. To address this, we developed a clinically translatable, fully synthetic nerve conduit that aligns with native regenerative principles through hierarchical microtopological engineering and phase-specific molecular delivery.
